headline: [Chip Crackdown!] US Moves to Block China's [Remote Access] to AI Chips
sub: Licences now needed for overseas data centers
caption:
💻 Chip Crackdown! US Moves to Block China's Remote Access to AI Chips

The US Commerce Department announced a new rule on Monday, November 16, to stop Chinese companies from using advanced American AI chips remotely through data centers in other countries. Selling these chips directly to China already needs a US licence.

🔹 Data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil will now need a US licence to receive advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other US makers. US-based companies operating there are exempt.
🔹 Exporters and data center operators must check that no company from China or other restricted countries is controlling or using the computing power, including through middlemen.
🔹 The move comes days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down over reports linking him to a woman US officials reportedly suspected of being a Chinese operative. Nvidia reports its earnings on Tuesday.
